body.p: Favorable reconsideration of this application is respectfully requested in view of the following remarks.

Claims 1-4, 10, 11, and 14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0093226 to Dr Moschos in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0077093 to Pan, U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0110444 to Sherwood et al., and U.S. Patent No. 10,195,147 to Yadidi.

Further, claim 5 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U. S. Patent Application Publication No. 2010/0292601 to Dompeling et al.; claims 6 and 7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, Dompeling, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0035326 to King-Smith; claims 8 and 9 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, Dompeling, King-Smith, U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0119280 to Ahmad et al., and International Patent Application Publication No. WO 2018/071441 to Akouka et al.; claim 13 stands rejected under 35 U. S. C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U. S. Patent Application Publication No. 2016/0338616 to Eichler; claim 15 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0173731 to Meka et al.; claim 16 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2012/0004571 to Ku et al.; claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U. S. C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2015/0072889 to Lui et al.; claim 18 stands rejected under 35 U. S. C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U.S. Patent No. 5,465,728 to Phillips; and claims 19-21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0138577 to Kline.
The rejection is respectfully traversed for at least the following reasons.

Independent claim 1 recites, in combination with other features, a sample delivery part that comprises an air diverter arranged to divide the sample delivery part into an upstream portion and a downstream portion. A breath sampler having at least this feature in combination with the other features set forth in claim 1 is neither derivable from nor rendered obvious by the cited references.

The Official Action acknowledges that Dr Moschos does not disclose the recited air diverter, and therefore, further cites Sherwood to supposedly remedy the deficiency (See Official Action, top of page 10 and the first paragraph on page 11).

Sherwood concerns a gas sampling device that includes a diverter valve (1050) or other component that is configured to selectively route exhaled air to either the exhaust post (1054) or the gas testing chamber (1026) (see para. [0086]). As is clear from at least Fig. 10 of Sherwood, the diverter valve is movable between two different positions - a first position, as illustrated in Fig. 10, that blocks the exhaled air from entering the gas chamber (1026) and permitting passage of the exhaled air through the exhaust port (1054); and a second position, as indicated by the arrow on the air diverter in Fig. 10, that permits entry of the exhaled air into the gas chamber (1026) and blocks the exhaled air from passing through the exhaust port (1054). Sherwood also explains that this arrangement is advantageous so that the patient's exhaled air is sampled at an optimum point (see para. [0087], which provides "the data collected by the sensor 1052 can dictate whether the exhaled air is exhausted from the housing 1020 or collected as sample gas in the gas testing chamber 1026. For example, the CO2 content of the air from the patient can be monitored and the exhaled air can be diverted to the gas testing chamber 1026 when the CO2 content plateaus").

Based on Sherwood, the Official Action has taken the position that it would have been obvious to substitute the wall (dividing member 128) of Dr Moschos for the diverter valve of Sherwood to selectively route air (See Official Action, bottom of page 12). However, if the ordinary skilled person were to have modified Dr Moschos' exhaled breath condensate collection device to have Sherwood's diverter valve in place of the dividing member as proposed by the Official Action, the diverter valve would necessarily interfere with the flow path of an exhaled breath through Dr Moschos device.

In particular, the dividing member of Dr Moschos divides the breath sampler into the first chamber 130 and the second chamber (i.e., non-rebreather part and sample delivery part) and not the second chamber (sample delivery part) into two parts like the air diverter of claim 1. Substituting the diverter valve for the dividing member would modify the boundary between the

two chambers and would necessarily affect the flow of air from the breath inlet tube 132 to the breath outlet port 124. More specifically, arranging the diverter valve in place of the dividing member would either permit the exhaled breath to flow normally (as intended in Dr Moschos) from the breath inlet port 122 through the breath outlet port 124 (when the diverter valve is in the first position that blocks the exhaled air from entering the gas chamber and permits passage of the exhaled air through the exhaust port) or block the exhaled breath from flowing through the breath outlet port 124 entirely (when the diverter vale is in the second position that permits entry of the exhaled air into the gas chamber and blocks the exhaled air from passing through the exhaust post).

Given that both the sample delivery part (second chamber of annotated Fig. la) and the exhaust (exhaust outlet port 140) are arranged downstream of the dividing member in Dr Moschos, substituting the diverter valve in place of the dividing member would also not have the same intended effect as Sherwood's diverter valve, i.e. selectively routing the exhaled air to one of the exhaust port or the gas testing chamber. Not to mention, the second position of the diverter valve (that blocks the exhaled breath from passing through the exhaust port) would be problematic since an exhaled breath would be blocked from flowing through the breath outlet port (124) and would have no other way of exiting from the device apart from through the point of entry therein (at breath inlet port 122).

For at least these reasons, it is respectfully submitted that even if the ordinary skilled person had been equipped with Sherwood, if and when seeking to modify the exhaled breath condensate collection device of Dr Moschos, he/she still would not have been directed to arrive at the breath sampler set forth in claim 1. Further, Pan and Yadidi both fail to teach or suggest the recited air diverter, and as such, neither document can reasonably be applied to remedy the aforementioned deficiencies of Dr Moschos and Sherwood.

For the sake of completeness, it is recognized that Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline were also cited by the Official Action but solely with respect to features set forth in dependent claims. Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline each lack any disclosure or reasonable suggestion of the recited air diverter. Consequently, none of Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline can be applied to remedy the aforementioned deficiencies of Dr Moschos, Pan, Sherwood, and Yadidi.

For at least the reasons discussed herein, it is respectfully submitted that the disclosures in Dr Moschos, Pan, Sherwood, Yadidi, Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline, whether taken individually or in combination, would not have rendered the breath sampler set forth in claim 1 obvious.

The dependent claims are patentable over the cited references at least by virtue of their dependence from independent claim 1. A detailed discussion of the additional distinguishing features recited in the dependent claims is thus not set forth at this time. Applicant reserves the right to present such arguments later during prosecution or appeal.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.

Early and favorable action with respect to this application is respectfully requested. In view of the above amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all of the claims now pending in the instant application should be allowable, and reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.

Respectfully submitted,
